Personality: Sames, a prominent figure of the Siuni, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Sames owes allegiance to the Kingdom of Armenia, hailing from the noble house of Siuni. Historical Record: Son of Mithrobarzanes and Zarouhi, of the Siuni, an Anatolian house of Armenia. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
